transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for your help. Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So gardening is fine as part of light exercise once that first week is over.

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise, as well as lifting heavy objects, for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for letting me know. I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. It's safe to continue using any eye drops or gels you were using before your operation, such as for dry eyes. So you can go ahead and use your eye gel again.

If you do run out, your GP should be able to provide you with more.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know, thank you. I'm also very sensitive to bright light now. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please get in touch with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation, but this should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? That will help me give you a better idea of what to expect.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's been about a week since my surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's helpful to know. Since it's been about a week, some blurriness is still quite normal at this stage. Your vision should improve quickly over the coming days and weeks.

However, if your vision is still blurry or gets significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that covers all my questions. Thank you so much for all the information, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered everything I wanted to know. Thank you again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! I'm so glad I could help. Take care, and best of luck with your recovery!

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn starting "It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light...". However, the `escalation_criteria` point was not conveyed at any point in the conversation.
